data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's gross claims outstanding at 1 January (opening reserves) were GBP 123.693m. Analysis of the gross claims development table indicates an adverse prior-year development (strengthening) of approximately GBP 27.7m (gross), primarily driven by adverse development on the 2016 and 2017 underwriting years. The report does not state an explicit gross prior-year movement in narrative; the figure above is calculated from the gross claims development triangle. Potential drivers noted in the report include adverse claims development, large-loss movements and reserving judgement/IBNR recalibration, with exposure concentrated in liability-related business.
raw_causal_phrases: The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.
Judgement is used to assess the extent to which past trends may not apply in the future.

The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' statement was found in the narrative. The prior-year development figure above was calculated from the gross claims development (triangle) (pages 37-38) by comparing current estimates to the previous diagonal for underwriting years 2016 and 2017 (excluding 2018 and 2019 as per guidance). No RITC distortion was identified. exact_reserve_text is empty because no verbatim sentence quantifying gross prior-year movement was present. Named 'events' listed are internal scenario stress tests included in the risk section, not historical catastrophe events.
